items_missed: No 'How are you today?', no agenda statement, no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never confirmed the full origin address or the destination address/zip on the call — worked off 'paramount way' pulled from her existing profile and never read either address back
Never asked about packing services or quoted packing pricing, even though she described loose blankets, totes, and boxes she hadn't finished packing
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — gave an 8:30-9:00 AM arrival window but never said Einstein discounts if it misses it
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — the single biggest miss on this call, because she hard-capped the crew at 2.5 hours and prep advice was the only lever that could make that cap actually work
No Ecobox referral despite an obvious materials need
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave hours or how to reach the branch
Roughly three minutes lost to the 'why does the system say you're a repeat customer' detour before any move details were gathered
top_strength: Best No Worries explanation of the batch — he tied it directly to her stated fear about the two mounted TVs, framed the 60 cents/lb state baseline as 'rather lackluster,' then laid out the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse coverage. He also handled the $165 competitor quote without a hint of defensiveness, walking her through weekday tiers, the third-mover math, and the per-15-minute rate until she chose to book.
coaching_note: When a customer caps the crew at 2.5 hours on a fourth-floor apartment with a 30-minute drive, that is the exact moment to run Save Your Ass — prep before move day is what makes her cap achievable and protects the estimate. Erik explained the risk but never gave her the tools to avoid it.
phone_presence_notes: Used 'Jessica' repeatedly and naturally, defused the awkward duplicate-profile moment with 'no worries at all, we're here now,' and met her TV anxiety with 'I totally understand those are fragile items' before pivoting into coverage.
